pages.title: Rooms
pages.content:
Four rooms, one wedding

Weavers' Hall offers four distinct daylit spaces for your wedding, transitioning naturally from the morning preparations to the midnight close. Every room is reserved exclusively for your celebration, with a quiet wet-weather plan always in place.

The North Room

A calm ceremony hall defined by morning light, oak chairs and lime-washed brick.

The North Room is our dedicated ceremony hall, seating up to 120 guests in simple pale oak chairs facing the tall arched windows. Consistent, gentle northern daylight illuminates the lime-washed brick walls and original 1908 timber floorboards, creating a luminous and unhurried atmosphere. Acoustically warm and free from direct glare, the room requires very little adornment beyond seasonal foliage. The handcrafted oak seating, aisle runners, and a minimalist timber signing table remain permanently in the space, ensuring that your ceremony unfolds in quiet architectural clarity.

Ceremonies up to 120 seated

The Long Hall

The main hall: long undyed-linen tables, oak seating, daylight turning to candlelight.

The Long Hall hosts seated wedding dinners for up to 96 guests along continuous undyed-linen tables. Seven tall windows line the southern elevation, filling the expansive wool-exchange room with shafts of river light before transitioning to warm ambient lamplight at dusk. The acoustics are intentionally tempered by the heavy linen drapery and lime plaster, allowing conversations to flow effortlessly from one end of the room to the other. Our solid oak banquet tables, simple oak dining chairs, and neutral linen runners remain in the room for every reception.

Dinner for up to 96 at long tables

The Garden Court

A gravel courtyard behind old brick walls, with olive trees in planters and warm festoon bulbs.

Enclosed by historic weathered brick and the river warehouse facade, the Garden Court accommodates up to 140 guests for afternoon drinks, relaxed conversation, and evening dancing. Crushed river gravel underfoot and two mature potted olive trees define the courtyard, while overhead festoon bulbs cast a warm glow as the sun sets over Calder Wharf. Low acoustic resonance against the exterior brick keeps music contained and intimate. Solid oak high tables, perimeter bench seating, and subtle festoon lighting remain fixtures of the courtyard throughout the season.

Drinks and dancing for up to 140

The Dressing Room

A private suite away from the public rooms, open to the wedding party from 11:00.

Available from 11:00 on the morning of your wedding, the Dressing Room provides a calm private sanctuary for up to 8 people. Positioned in the quietest wing of the building, the room is bathed in gentle morning daylight from an original multi-pane sash window. Soft acoustic insulation shields you from the preparations elsewhere in the hall. A full-length timber-framed mirror, comfortable upholstered armchairs, an oak garment rail, and low side tables remain in the room to keep your preparations comfortable and completely unhurried.

For up to 8, from 11:00

Wet-Weather Transition

When rain or sudden river winds arise, outdoor ceremonies move from the Garden Court into the North Room in exactly 20 minutes. Tomas Achterberg and our dedicated house team execute this transition quietly in the background, rearranging seating, transferring floral displays, and lighting candles without causing any disruption to you or your guests. Having an equally beautiful indoor ceremony setting already prepared ensures you can relax completely, knowing your timeline remains entirely protected regardless of changing weather along the wharf.

Included

Tables, oak chairs, undyed linen and glassware for up to 96 at dinner.

The house team for the whole hire, 11:00 to 00:30: Amara on the day, Rafael at the bar, Tomas for the building. Heating, a step-free route to every room, and a cloakroom by the main doors.

Fees & Dates

pages.title: The Day
pages.content:
A wedding day as it actually runs

At Kasane Venue, only one wedding takes place each day, allowing our riverside hall to operate on an unhurried, natural rhythm. From the opening of the doors at 11:00 to our quiet midnight close, every moment unfolds seamlessly.

Morning to midnight

Every wedding here follows the same frame, so you can plan around it and change what you like. Amara keeps the schedule and the running order, and she meets you three times beforehand: six months, eight weeks and ten days before the day.

11:00At 11:00, the doors of Weavers' Hall open exclusively for the wedding party. You have private access to the Dressing Room to begin getting ready, unpack personal items, and share quiet morning refreshments. Amara Okonjo and the house team are already on site, receiving deliveries from Hana Kowalczyk and ensuring all tables and ceremony chairs are impeccably arranged.
13:00Guests begin arriving at Calder Wharf from 13:00, stepping through the double doors into the open air of the Garden Court. Welcome drinks and chilled water are served among the potted olive trees while friends and family reconnect on the crushed river gravel. The courtyard provides an unhurried transition before everyone is invited inside for the marriage ceremony.
14:00At 14:00, guests take their seats in the North Room or the Garden Court for the marriage vows. Soft daylight pours through the tall arched windows, framing the ceremony against the quiet lime-washed brickwork. When celebrations take place outside, guests shower the couple exclusively with biodegradable dried flower petals, preserving the clean natural character of our courtyard and the surrounding riverside wharf.
15:00Following the ceremony at 15:00, the wedding party gathers in the Garden Court for celebratory drinks, light aperitifs, and photographs. The double doors to the hall stand open, creating a gentle indoor-outdoor flow between the gravel courtyard and the shaded interior. Guests can wander freely, take in views of Calder Wharf, and relax while the kitchen team finalises dinner preparations.
18:30Dinner is served at 18:30 in the Long Hall, where guests gather around undyed-linen banquet tables under warm evening light. Lucien Marchetti and the kitchen serve a three-course seasonal menu highlighting fresh local produce. Table candles are permitted in enclosed holders to protect the undyed linen, creating an intimate, shared dining experience that extends naturally into the evening.
21:00At 21:00, banquet tables are smoothly shifted back by the house team to reveal a generous oak dance floor in the hall. Rafael Duarte opens the bar, pouring craft beers, natural wines, and seasonal cocktails as evening music begins. The Garden Court remains warmly lit with overhead festoons for guests seeking cool night air and quiet conversation beneath the stars.
23:30In accordance with our quiet riverside noise limits, all live music and amplified sound conclude promptly at 23:30. The final hour provides a calm, unhurried winding down, allowing guests to finish their drinks, collect coats from the Dressing Room, and say their evening goodbyes under the soft amber glow of the hall lanterns before heading out onto Calder Wharf.
00:30At 00:30, the wedding hire period concludes and the double doors of Weavers' Hall are closed for the night. Taxis meet departing guests outside 22 Calder Wharf, while the house team secures the building. Any personal styling decor, gifts, and clothing safely left in the Dressing Room can be collected during next-morning brunch or by arrangement with Priya Nair.

If the weather turns

Every outdoor moment has an indoor twin.

The ceremony can move from the Garden Court to the North Room in twenty minutes, and drinks move to the Long Hall with the double doors left open. Elif and Jonah had 92 guests and an October downpour; nobody was in the wrong room at the wrong time.

Decided by 12:00 on the day

Smaller days, winter days

The same day, quieter.

A Monday to Thursday wedding or a winter day often means fewer guests. Sanne and Theo had 34 around one candlelit table on a January Tuesday. The hire, the hours and the house team are the same; only the fee changes.

Winter day from €5,200

pages.title: Food
pages.content:
One kitchen, cooked in the building

Our culinary offering is centered around an in-house kitchen that values seasonal ingredients, simple presentation, and generous hospitality. From candlelit dinners to garden brunches, every menu is crafted specifically for Weavers' Hall.

Dinner

Head of the kitchen Lucien Marchetti guides our culinary program with a focus on regional, seasonal ingredients and straightforward culinary technique. We do not permit outside caterers, ensuring that every dish is prepared fresh on site to the highest standard. Our signature three-course dinner is priced at €118 per guest, including artisan bread, seasonal starters, hearty main courses, and delicate desserts. Dishes are designed to be served family-style or individually plated along our long undyed-linen tables, encouraging lively conversation and relaxed dining throughout the evening.

At the table

Linen, glass, bread and a short menu.

We believe every guest should dine with equal pleasure and complete peace of mind. Lucien Marchetti customises wedding menus to accommodate vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, and specific allergy requirements when notified during our planning sessions with Amara Okonjo. While external catering companies are not permitted at Kasane Venue, couples are entirely welcome to bring their own bespoke wedding cake or artisan celebration desserts from outside bakers, which our kitchen team will slice and present without any plating fees.

Three courses, €118 per guest

The next morning

A brunch in the Garden Court for those who stay.

For couples extending their gathering into the following day, Lucien offers an informal next-morning brunch in the Garden Court at €34 per guest. Served between 10:00 and 13:00, the menu features freshly baked sourdough loaves, seasonal fruit, cultured butter, regional cheeses, and warm filter coffee. Guests can gather on the sunlit gravel under the olive trees to relive moments from the previous night in a peaceful, unhurried atmosphere before concluding their celebrations and departing from Calder Wharf.

Brunch, €34 per guest

The evening bar

Run by Rafael until the music ends at 23:30.

Rafael Duarte oversees the evening bar and hospitality, curating a thoughtful list of low-intervention wines, local craft beers, spirits, and non-alcoholic infusions. Rafael works directly with couples during their planning phase to select beverage pairings that complement Lucien's dinner menu. Operating from 15:00 until music concludes at 23:30, the bar provides attentive, friendly service without long queues, ensuring glasses remain topped whether guests are mingling in the Garden Court or dancing across the oak floors.

pages.title: Fees & Dates
pages.content:
What the hall costs

We maintain clear, transparent pricing with no hidden charges, giving you exclusive access to Weavers' Hall for the entirety of your wedding day. All listed fees include VAT, furniture, linen, and our dedicated house team.

Hire 11:00 to 00:30

Every private hire booking grants exclusive access to the Weavers' Hall and Garden Court from 11:00 until 00:30. Your fee includes handcrafted oak dining and ceremony chairs, solid timber banquet tables, natural undyed-linen table runners, and dedicated staffing throughout the day. Co-founder Tomas Achterberg coordinates facilities on site, Amara Okonjo manages your operational timeline, and our house team handles complete setup and post-event cleaning, allowing you to enjoy your wedding entirely free from logistical burdens.

  • SaturdayApril–October€11,500
  • Friday or SundayApril–October€8,900
  • Monday–ThursdayApril–October€6,800
  • Winter dayany day, November–March€5,200

Extras

  • Ceremony onlyNorth Room, 2 hours, Monday–Thursday€2,400
  • Dinnerthree courses, per guest€118
  • Next-morning brunchGarden Court, per guest€34

Terms

Following an initial viewing with Priya Nair, couples may place a complimentary date hold on their preferred day for up to 7 days. To formally secure your date, we require a 30% non-refundable deposit alongside a signed hire agreement. The remaining 70% balance is due 8 weeks prior to your wedding day. In the event of cancellation more than 8 weeks before the event, the final balance is fully waived or refunded, while the initial deposit is retained to cover administrative costs.

Capacity: ceremony up to 120 seated, dinner up to 96, Garden Court up to 140 standing.

Dates Still Open This Year

Because we host only one wedding per day, our calendar fills steadily throughout the year. We currently have select midweek and weekend dates still available in the upcoming season, specifically across July, August, October, November, and December. If you have a specific month or seasonal window in mind, please reach out to Priya Nair with your preferred timeframe, and she will provide an up-to-date schedule of open days and arrange a private 60-minute walk through the hall.

Request a viewing

pages.title: The People
pages.content:
Seven people look after the building

Weavers' Hall is maintained and brought to life by a close-knit team dedicated to thoughtful hospitality and meticulous preservation. Get to know the seven people who guide your wedding from first viewing to the final song.

The team

  • Ines VargaCo-Founder and Venue DirectorInes Varga co-founded Kasane Venue in spring 2016 following a two-year architectural restoration of the 1908 wool exchange. As venue director, Ines oversees the artistic direction, operational standards, and long-term vision of Weavers' Hall. Her focus on calm aesthetics and single-event exclusivity ensures every wedding feels personal, beautifully paced, and deeply respectful of the building's historic fabric.
  • Tomas AchterbergCo-Founder and Keeper of the BuildingTomas Achterberg co-founded the venue alongside Ines and serves as the dedicated keeper of the building. With an intimate knowledge of Weavers' Hall's timber framing and mechanical systems, Tomas personally oversees building conservation, morning room arrangements, atmospheric lighting transitions, and our 20-minute wet-weather plans, ensuring the historic venue functions effortlessly in every season.
  • Amara OkonjoWedding CoordinatorAmara Okonjo is your dedicated wedding coordinator and primary contact throughout the entire planning process. From your initial booking confirmation through the final song at 23:30, Amara leads three structured planning meetings at six months, eight weeks, and ten days prior to your wedding, coordinating suppliers, timelines, and logistics so you can remain entirely relaxed.
  • Priya NairBookings and ViewingsPriya Nair manages all initial inquiries, calendar dates, and private viewings at 22 Calder Wharf. Priya welcomes couples for their 60-minute walk through the hall, answering practical questions about capacities, pricing, and ceremony setups. She also oversees our monthly open days on the first Saturday of each month, helping prospective couples explore the spaces at their own pace.
  • Lucien MarchettiHead of the KitchenLucien Marchetti leads our on-site kitchen, bringing an ingredient-driven philosophy to wedding dining. Lucien designs seasonal three-course banquet menus priced at €118 per guest, alongside leisurely next-morning brunches at €34 per guest. Working closely with regional growers, he ensures every dish served in the Long Hall or Garden Court is fresh, vibrant, and tailored to dietary needs.
  • Hana KowalczykFlorist in ResidenceHana Kowalczyk is our resident floral designer, working from her studio near Calder Wharf to create botanical arrangements that complement the hall's natural daylight and undyed linen. Hana sources local seasonal stems, architectural branches, and delicate dried petals for courtyard confetti, crafting bespoke ceremonial arches, dining runners, and bouquets that blend harmoniously with our historic lime-washed walls.
  • Rafael DuarteEvening Host and BarRafael Duarte manages evening hospitality and bar operations at Kasane Venue, ensuring drinks service runs seamlessly from the post-ceremony reception until the music concludes at 23:30. Rafael curates our selection of natural wines, craft beers, and bespoke cocktails, managing glassware and beverage pacing while maintaining a warm, hospitable atmosphere across the hall and Garden Court.

One wedding a day

Why the team is small.

We host one wedding a day on purpose. Everyone on the team is in the building from 11:00 to the last guest, and everyone knows your names, your order of the day and which cousin needs the step-free route.

pages.title: The Building
pages.content:
A wool exchange, built in 1908

Standing on the banks of Calder Wharf, Weavers' Hall is a former industrial wool exchange that has been sensitively restored into a calm, daylit wedding venue. Its layered history is reflected in original oak timber, lime plaster, and fourteen tall windows.

The 1908 Wool Exchange on Calder Wharf

Constructed in 1908 during the industrial height of Halbrook's textile trade, Weavers' Hall originally served as a bustling wool exchange and trading floor. Raw fleeces and spun wool were weighed, graded, and traded beneath its high ceilings, where fourteen tall arched windows were specifically oriented to capture consistent daylight for quality inspection. The generous proportions, robust brickwork, and structural integrity of the original Edwardian build provided an exceptional architectural foundation that still defines the space today.

As commercial textile trading shifted away from Halbrook's waterways in the mid-twentieth century, the building transitioned to light industrial storage in 1971. For over three decades, wooden crates and surplus materials filled the hall, obscuring its tall windows and architectural character. By 2003, the warehouse was locked and left entirely vacant, standing quietly beside Calder Wharf for ten years until Ines Varga and Tomas Achterberg discovered the neglected property in late 2013.

Daylight did the work first.

Fourteen windows, laid out for one wedding a day.

The hall

Fourteen windows, an oak floor and lime-washed walls.

Between 2014 and 2016, Ines and Tomas embarked on a meticulous two-year restoration to revive Weavers' Hall. Rather than modernising the building with synthetic surfaces, the restoration prioritized traditional craftsmanship and breathable natural materials. The original solid oak floorboards were carefully lifted, cleaned, and re-laid, while the interior brickwork was treated with breathable lime wash. All fourteen tall multi-pane windows were meticulously restored, filling the voluminous hall with soft, natural river daylight once again.

Built 1908 · restored 2014–2016

Opening as Kasane Venue in Spring 2016

The doors open straight out.

Weavers' Hall officially opened its doors as Kasane Venue in spring 2016, dedicated exclusively to hosting weddings. Guided by the principle of holding only one event per day, the founders established an unhurried sanctuary where couples could gather with their loved ones. Today, the building seamlessly combines century-old textile heritage with discreet modern infrastructure, offering a calm, timeless setting where new histories are created each week along the wharf.

pages.title: Viewings
pages.content:
Come and walk through the hall

We invite you to experience the natural light and calm proportions of Weavers' Hall firsthand before choosing your wedding date. Private 60-minute appointments and monthly open days allow you to explore the spaces without pressure.

Walking Weavers' Hall with Priya

Private viewings at Kasane Venue are hosted by Priya Nair and last approximately 60 minutes. During your walk, Priya guides you through the North Room, Long Hall, Dressing Room, and Garden Court, explaining how the light moves across the brickwork throughout the day. You will discuss seasonal timing, dining layouts, acoustic qualities, and our 20-minute wet-weather plan. Viewings are offered Tuesday through Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 by appointment, ensuring you have the entire venue to yourselves.

The Five Booking Steps

Securing your wedding at Kasane Venue follows five straightforward steps. First, request a viewing by email. Second, walk the building with Priya Nair during a 60-minute private appointment. Third, place a complimentary hold on your preferred wedding date for up to 7 days. Fourth, formally confirm your date by signing the agreement and paying the 30% deposit. Fifth, attend three scheduled planning meetings with coordinator Amara Okonjo at six months, eight weeks, and ten days before your celebration.

Request a viewing

Write to Priya with two or three possible days.

To request a private viewing, email us at hello@kasanevenue.example with your preferred date range, anticipated guest count, and whether you envision an indoor or outdoor ceremony. We also host an informal open day on the first Saturday of every month from 11:00 to 15:00, where no appointment is required. During open days, Weavers' Hall is dressed with undyed linen and seasonal florals, allowing you to walk through the spaces freely at your own leisure.

pages.title: Visit & Contact
pages.content:
Weavers' Hall, Calder Wharf

Kasane Venue is situated at Weavers' Hall along the quiet riverside of Calder Wharf in Halbrook. Whether arriving by train or car, our riverside location offers straightforward access and step-free convenience for all guests.

Getting here

You will find Kasane Venue at Weavers' Hall, 22 Calder Wharf, Halbrook. For guests arriving by rail, the venue is an easy 12-minute level walk along the scenic river wharf from Halbrook train station. For those travelling by automobile, we provide 18 dedicated on-site parking spaces directly adjacent to the hall, including designated bays for loading and accessible parking. Additional public vehicle parking is available within a short walk along the riverside.

Hours

Our administrative office operates Tuesday through Friday from 9:30 to 17:30 to handle planning inquiries and supplier coordination. Private viewings are conducted Tuesday through Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 by prior appointment, alongside our open day on the first Saturday of each month between 11:00 and 15:00. The venue is closed on Mondays, except when reserved exclusively for that day's wedding party. For all inquiries, please email our team at hello@kasanevenue.example.

  • Viewingsby appointmentTue–Sun 10:00–17:00
  • Open dayfirst Saturday of every month11:00–15:00
  • Officeby emailTue–Fri 9:30–17:30
  • Wedding hireone wedding a day11:00–00:30

Access

Weavers' Hall offers full step-free access across all ground-floor spaces, including the North Room, Long Hall, Dressing Room, Garden Court, and accessible washroom facilities. Guests requiring level entry can navigate the entire property comfortably without encountering steps or narrow barriers. For overnight stays, Halbrook offers several charming riverside guesthouses, boutique town inns, and comfortable bed-and-breakfasts situated within a convenient five to fifteen-minute walk or taxi ride from Calder Wharf.

pages.title: Questions
pages.content:
Questions couples ask

Here are answers to the questions couples ask most frequently when planning their wedding at Weavers' Hall. If you need further clarification regarding our spaces or services, our team is always pleased to assist.

Before you book

What is the guest capacity across the venue?

Weavers' Hall comfortably accommodates wedding celebrations of varying sizes across its four spaces. The North Room seats up to 120 guests for indoor ceremonies. The Long Hall seats up to 96 guests along long undyed-linen banquet tables for dinner. The Garden Court accommodates up to 140 guests standing for open-air drinks receptions and evening dancing, while the private Dressing Room provides ample space for up to 8 people during morning preparations.

Do you host more than one wedding a day?

No, we strictly host only one wedding per day. When you book Kasane Venue, Weavers' Hall and the Garden Court are exclusively yours from 11:00 in the morning until 00:30 at night. There are no overlapping events, no shared corridors, and no hurried turnarounds. Our entire staff, from coordinator Amara Okonjo to the kitchen and bar teams, is dedicated entirely to your celebration.

What are the rules regarding music and evening sound?

To respect our tranquil riverside location and local municipal noise guidelines, all live bands, DJs, and amplified sound must conclude promptly at 23:30. Acoustic background music is welcomed earlier in the day across both the hall and Garden Court. From 23:30 until doors close at 00:30, guests can finish drinks and conversation under lowered ambient lighting as the evening comes to a gentle close.

Are real candles permitted inside the hall?

Real candles are warmly welcomed throughout Weavers' Hall to create an intimate atmosphere, provided they are safely enclosed within glass storm lanterns, glass holders, or hurricane vases. To protect our handcrafted undyed-linen table runners and original oak floors, open naked flames without wax catchers are strictly prohibited on dining tables. Our team will happily review your candle vessels during your planning meeting with Amara.

Is Weavers' Hall fully accessible for all guests?

Yes, Weavers' Hall is designed with comprehensive step-free access throughout the premises. The main entrance, North Room, Long Hall, Dressing Room, and Garden Court are all situated on the ground level, featuring wide doorways and smooth thresholds. Accessible, step-free washrooms are conveniently located adjacent to the main hall, and dedicated accessible vehicle parking spaces are situated directly next to the venue entrance.

Are children welcome at the venue?

Children are warmly welcomed at Kasane Venue. The enclosed boundary of the Garden Court and the self-contained layout of Weavers' Hall provide a safe, secure environment for families. Head chef Lucien Marchetti is pleased to prepare simplified, child-friendly dining portions upon request, and our spacious Dressing Room can serve as a quiet retreat for young children or nursing parents throughout the afternoon and evening.

What happens if it rains during an outdoor ceremony?

If you plan an outdoor ceremony in the Garden Court and rain or inclement weather arrives, we activate our 20-minute wet-weather plan. Tomas Achterberg and our house team will seamlessly relocate your ceremony into the daylit North Room, transferring floral arrangements and arranging oak seating without delaying your timeline. Both spaces remain fully reserved for you, ensuring a seamless and stress-free alternative.

Can we bring our own suppliers and caterers?

All dining at Kasane Venue is prepared exclusively on site by our house kitchen under head chef Lucien Marchetti; outside catering companies are not permitted. However, you are entirely welcome to bring your own wedding cake or patisserie from an external baker. For floristry, photography, and music, you may choose independent suppliers or work with our resident florist Hana Kowalczyk.

How much is the deposit and when is the balance due?

To secure your chosen wedding date, we require a 30% deposit upon signing the venue hire agreement, following a complimentary 7-day date hold. The remaining 70% balance, alongside final guest counts and catering choices, is due exactly 8 weeks prior to your wedding day. Payments are processed securely via bank transfer in EUR, with full VAT invoices provided for every transaction.

What is your cancellation policy?

If you need to cancel your booking more than 8 weeks prior to your wedding date, any balance payments made beyond the initial deposit will be fully refunded, though the 30% deposit is retained to cover scheduling and administration. Cancellations made within 8 weeks of the wedding date are non-refundable, as dates cannot be reallocated on such short notice. We recommend taking out wedding insurance.

posts.title: An Autumn Saturday along Calder Wharf: Elif and Jonah at Weavers' Hall
posts.excerpt: On a quiet October Saturday, ninety-two guests gathered at Weavers' Hall for Elif and Jonah's wedding, where shifting autumn rain and candlelit linen tables shaped an unhurried riverside celebration.
posts.content:
The October morning arrived over Halbrook with low river mist and a steady, quiet breeze along Calder Wharf. At 11:00, the tall doors of Weavers' Hall opened for Elif and Jonah, marking the beginning of their wedding day. Having walked through the former 1908 wool exchange with Priya Nair earlier in the spring, the couple had fallen in love with the building's honest textures—the lime-washed brickwork, the fourteen grand arched windows, and the quiet rhythm of hosting only one wedding a day. In the Dressing Room, bathed in soft morning light, Elif prepared alongside her closest friends while Tomas Achterberg and wedding coordinator Amara Okonjo completed the final touches in the main hall.

By 13:00, ninety-two guests began arriving through the wharf gates into the Garden Court. Beneath two mature olive trees, friends embraced over chilled welcome drinks while crushed river gravel crunched underfoot. Although the ceremony was originally envisioned for the open courtyard, the autumn clouds darkened suddenly over the water. Without a moment of hesitation or unease, Amara and Tomas initiated the venue's twenty-minute wet-weather transition. Oak chairs were quietly transferred indoors, glass lanterns were arranged along the aisle, and by 14:00, guests took their seats inside the warm, luminous North Room as steady rain began pattering against the historic glass.

Exchanging vows framed by the tall northern windows proved to be one of the day's most breathtaking moments. The lime plaster walls softened the room's acoustics, lending an intimate, reverent stillness to the ceremony. Hana Kowalczyk, the venue's resident florist, had dressed the aisle with understated arrangements of seasonal branches, dried seed heads, and trailing foliage that echoed the wild plants along the riverbank. When the couple walked down the aisle as husband and wife, cheers resonated through the hall, unbothered by the storm outside.

As the rain cleared into a soft grey afternoon at 15:00, guests drifted back into the Garden Court for drinks and relaxed conversation, the hall's double doors standing wide open to link the indoor and outdoor spaces. At 18:30, the celebration moved into the Long Hall for dinner. One continuous banquet table, draped in heavy undyed linen and illuminated by hundreds of flickering table candles, stretched down the center of the oak floorboards. Head chef Lucien Marchetti presented a three-course seasonal feast priced at €118 per guest, featuring crusty artisan sourdough, roasted autumnal roots, tender braised meats, and delicate spiced fruit desserts.

As evening fell, Rafael Duarte took charge of the bar, pouring biodynamic wines, local craft beers, and bespoke botanical cocktails. At 21:00, the house team effortlessly moved the banquet tables back to open the expansive oak floor for dancing. For the next two and a half hours, the historic wool exchange echoed with music and celebration. At 23:30, in accordance with the hall's riverside curfew, the music drew to a graceful close, giving way to quiet goodbyes and laughter over final drinks under the festoon lights. By 00:30, the double doors were locked, bringing a perfectly paced, unforgettable autumn day to its natural rest.

posts.title: Sanne & Theo
posts.excerpt: A quiet winter Tuesday for 34 guests, gathered around one candlelit table.
posts.content:
Sanne and Theo married on a January Tuesday with 34 guests. On winter days the hall is hired from 11:00 to 00:30 like any other, but with fewer people the dinner was laid as one short table beneath the tall windows.

By 16:30 the windows had turned blue and the candles were lit. Lucien sent out three courses of winter vegetables and slow-cooked lamb, and the music ended early, well before the 23:30 limit.

posts.title: Marisol & Ade
posts.excerpt: A June garden ceremony for 120 guests with dried petals under bright summer skies.
posts.content:
Marisol and Ade married in the Garden Court in June with 120 guests, the most the courtyard holds standing. Hana dressed the olive trees in dried petals, which are the only confetti allowed on the gravel.

After the ceremony the party moved through the open double doors into the Long Hall for dinner, and came back outside at 21:00 when the tables were moved back and the dancing began.
